arxiv-1909-02992.title: A proof of N. Takahashi’s conjecture for ( ℙ 2 , E ) (\mathbb{P}^{2},E) and a refined sheaves/Gromov-Witten correspondence Mathematics Subject Classification: 14N35
arxiv-1909-02992.creator: Pierrick Bousseau
arxiv-1909-02992.description: Abstract . We prove N. Takahashi’s conjecture determining the contribution of each contact point in genus- 0 0 maximal contact Gromov–Witten theory of ℙ 2 \mathbb{P}^{2} relative to a smooth cubic E E . This is a new example of a question in Gromov–Witten theory which can be fully solved despite the presence of contracted components and multiple covers.

arxiv-2107-13449.title: Self-Learning Emulators and Eigenvector Continuation
arxiv-2107-13449.creator: Avik Sarkar, Dean Lee
arxiv-2107-13449.description: Abstract Emulators that can bypass computationally expensive scientific calculations with high accuracy and speed can enable new studies of fundamental science as well as more potential applications. In this work we discuss solving a system of constraint equations efficiently using a self-learning emulator.

arxiv-2211-16130.title: Strichartz estimates for Maxwell equations in media: the fully anisotropic case
arxiv-2211-16130.creator: Robert Schippa, Roland Schnaubelt
arxiv-2211-16130.description: Abstract . We prove Strichartz estimates for Maxwell equations in media in the fully anisotropic case with Hölder-continuous coefficients. To this end, we use the FBI transform to conjugate the problem to phase space. After reducing to a scalar estimate by means of a matrix symmetrizer, we show oscillatory integral estimates for a variable-coefficient Fourier extension operator.

arxiv-2403-05883.title: Precision premium transformation – a high-precision astrometric solution based on the precision premium curve
arxiv-2403-05883.creator: Z.J. Zheng, Q.Y. Peng, F.R. Lin, D. Li, Y. Zheng
arxiv-2403-05883.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Z.J. Zheng, Q.Y. Peng, F.R. Lin, D. Li, Y. Zheng. In Gaia era, atmospheric turbulence, which causes stochastic wander of a star image, is a fundamental limitation to the astrometric accuracy of ground-based optical imaging. However, the positional bias caused by turbulence (called turbulence error here) can be effectively reduced by measuring a target relative to another reference (a star or a fast-moving target) which locates in the range of only several tens of arcsec, since they suffer from similar turbulence errors.

arxiv-2405-09203.title: Monte Carlo on compact complex manifolds using Bergman kernels
arxiv-2405-09203.creator: Thibaut Lemoine, Rémi Bardenet
arxiv-2405-09203.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thibaut Lemoine, Rémi Bardenet. In this paper, we propose a new randomized method for numerical integration on a compact complex manifold with respect to a continuous volume form. Taking for quadrature nodes a suitable determinantal point process, we build an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator of the integral of any 𝒞 1 \mathscr{C}^{1} function, and show that the estimator satisfies a central limit theorem, with a faster rate than under independent sampling.

arxiv-2411-15520.title: Quiver presentations and Schur–Weyl duality for Khovanov arc algebras
arxiv-2411-15520.creator: C. Bowman, M. De Visscher, A. Dell’Arciprete, A. Hazi, R. Muth, C. Stroppel
arxiv-2411-15520.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by C. Bowman, M. De Visscher, A. Dell’Arciprete, A. Hazi, R. Muth, C. Stroppel. We provide an Ext {\rm Ext} -quiver and relations presentation of the Khovanov arc algebras and prove a precise analogue of the Kleshchev–Martin conjecture in this setting. Introduction

H^{m}_{n}
, were first introduced by Khovanov (in the case

arxiv-2506-08699.title: ArrowPose: Segmentation, Detection, and 5 DoF Pose Estimation Network for Colorless Point Clouds Thanks: This project was funded in part by Innovation Fund Denmark through the projects MADE ReAct and FERA, and in part by the SDU I4.0-Lab.
arxiv-2506-08699.creator: 1 st Frederik Hagelskjær
arxiv-2506-08699.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by 1 st Frederik Hagelskjær. This paper presents a fast detection and 5 DoF (Degrees of Freedom) pose estimation network for colorless point clouds. The pose estimation is calculated from center and top points of the object, predicted by the neural network. The network is trained on synthetic data, and tested on a benchmark dataset, where it demonstrates state-of-the-art performance and outperforms all colorless methods. The network is able to run inference in only 250 milliseconds making it usable in many scenarios.

arxiv-2507-06128.title: Geometric Invariants of Quantum Metrology
arxiv-2507-06128.creator: Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, Murray J. Holland
arxiv-2507-06128.description: Abstract We establish a previously unexplored conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) expressed as follows; when the QFIM is constructed from a set of observables closed under commutation, i.e., a Lie algebra, the spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under unitary dynamics generated by these same operators.

Infectious hypodermal and hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHHNV) is a widely distributed single-stranded DNA parvovirus that has been responsible for major losses in wild and farmed penaeid shrimp populations on the northwestern Pacific coast of Mexico since the early 1990's. IHHNV

pmc-10496220.title: Upper body compression wear improves muscle oxygenation following intense video game training: a randomized cross-over study among competitive gamers
pmc-10496220.creator: Joanne DiFrancisco-Donoghue, Alexander Rothstein, Min-Kyung Jung, Hallie Zwibel, William G Werner
pmc-10496220.description: BackgroundEsport players require a high number of action moves per minute to play, with substantial contractions of the wrist extensor muscles. Players frequently suffer from acute fatigue. The purpose of this study was to examine the use of below the elbow compression sleeves on Sm02 during intense aim training. Secondly, to examine players’ performance and perception with and without compression.

pmc-10738922.title: THE UNIQUE CHARACTERISTICS OF “FAMILIES OF CHOICE” AND BIOLOGICAL FAMILIES OF LGBT ADULTS
pmc-10738922.creator: Ella Cohn-Schwartz, Sigal Gooldin, Yaacov Bachner
pmc-10738922.description: This study joins a growing body of research on the unique families of aging individuals in sexual minorities. We explore the “families of choice” (who are close enough to be considered as family) and biological families of LGBT adults and their associations with mental health.

pmc-11449953.title: Genomic Validation in the UK Biobank Cohort Suggests a Role of C8B and MFG-E8 in the Pathogenesis of Trigeminal Neuralgia
pmc-11449953.creator: Muataz S Lafta, Gull Rukh, Sami Abu Hamdeh, Yasmina Molero, Aleksandr V Sokolov, Elham Rostami, Helgi B Schiöth
pmc-11449953.description: Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) is a severe facial pain disease of uncertain pathophysiology and unclear genetic background. Although recent research has reported a more important role of genetic factors in TN pathogenesis, few candidate genes have been proposed to date. The present study aimed to identify independent genetic variants in the protein-coding genes associated with TN.

pmc-11558219.title: Effects of HIV Self-Testing on Testing Promotion and Risk Behavior Reduction Among Transgender Women in China: Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-11558219.creator: Yan-Yan Zhu, Ze-Hao Ye, Zhen-Xing Chu, Yingjie Liu, Jie Wei, Le Jia, Yong-Jun Jiang, Hong Shang, Qing-Hai Hu, Amaryllis Mavragani, Allison Lale, Goulda Downer
pmc-11558219.description: BackgroundTo date, no randomized controlled trials have specifically addressed behavior changes after HIV self-testing (HIVST) among transgender women.ObjectiveThis study aims to evaluate the effects of HIVST on changes in HIV testing behavior, frequency of condomless sex, and partner numbers among transgender women in China.MethodsParticipants were recruited from 2 Chinese cities using both online and offline methods.

pmc-12430284.title: A Genome-Wide Modeling and Characterization Study of Pleckstrin Homology Domains in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
pmc-12430284.creator: Münevver Aksoy, Marina Krupitskaya, Shaneen M Singh, Michael Hippler, Shin-Ichiro Ozawa
pmc-12430284.description: The function of pleckstrin homology (PH) domains is to recognize and bind to specific phosphoinositides in the membranes as part of diverse cellular signaling processes. The structure of some PH domains has been solved by X-ray crystallography, but structures of many PH domains remain to be elucidated.

pmc-12437630.title: Ayahuasca and debut of psychosis, description of a clinical case
pmc-12437630.creator: E. E. Morales Castellano, P. Rivero Rodriguez, M. Martinez Grimal, J. J. Tascón Cervera, A. M. Morales Rivero
pmc-12437630.description: IntroductionThe relationship between psychosis and ayahuasca use is a topic of considerable interest and debate in the scientific and medical community. Ayahuasca is traditionally used in shamanic ceremonies in the Amazon, composed mainly of the Banisteriopsis caapi vine and the leaves of Psychotria viridis, which contain DMT (dimethyltryptamine), a powerful hallucinogen.

pmc-12656642.title: Effect of Drying Methods on the Morphological and Functional Properties of Cellulose Ester Films
pmc-12656642.creator: Tanuj Kattamanchi, Heikko Kallakas, Elvira Tarasova, Percy Festus Alao, Tiit Kaljuvee, Arvo Mere, Atanas Katerski, Rünno Lõhmus, Andres Krumme, Jaan Kers, Bin Li
pmc-12656642.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study presents the synthesis and characterisation of cellulose long chain fatty acid ester films using a novel distillable ionic liquid (IL), 5-methyl-1,5,7-triaza-bicyclo-[4.3.0] non-6-enium acetate [mTBNH][OAc] in combination with DMSO as a cosolvent. The cellulose esters cellulose diacetate (CDA), cellulose laurate (CL), and cellulose palmitate (CP) were fabricated through an evaporation-induced phase separation method (EIPS) and dried under two conditions: conventional oven drying (RO) and vacuum oven drying (VO).

pmc-12733103.title: Hypoxic Small Extracellular Vesicle Preconditioning of AC16 Cardiomyocytes Increase Caspase-3 and Caspase-8 Activity During Hypoxia
pmc-12733103.creator: Øystein Røsand, Victoria Johansen, Gurdeep Marwarha, Morten A Høydal, Manuela Zavatti, Francesca Beretti
pmc-12733103.description: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are increasingly recognized as crucial mediators of cell-cell communication. This study aims to determine the influence of sEV mediation on cardiomyocytes (CMs) under hypoxic conditions and identify the molecular modifications induced by hypoxia-derived sEVs (H-sEVs). Using a preconditional approach, we administered hypoxic AC16 CM-derived sEVs to recipient AC16 CMs before hypoxic stimulation.

pmc-13148652.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMeeting recruitment targets in an expeditious manner is essential to the successful completion of any research project. pmc-13410320.title: Heparin-Binding Protein and Transplant-Associated Inflammation: Emerging Roles in Infection, Ischemia–Reperfusion Injury, and Allograft Dysfunction
pmc-13410320.creator: Chengchang Zhang, Ruozhu Li, Chen Dai
pmc-13410320.description: Heparin-binding protein (HBP) is an activation-dependent neutrophil granule protein involved in innate immune activation, endothelial barrier disruption, and inflammatory tissue injury. Although HBP has been extensively investigated in infectious diseases, particularly sepsis, its potential relevance to transplantation has only recently attracted attention.

pmc-13448615.title: Use of cost analysis in examinations of health coaching interventions: a scoping review
pmc-13448615.creator: Maura Dougherty, Sophia M Bartels, Jason Smith, Steven Zeliadt, Justeen Hyde, Bo Kim
pmc-13448615.description: AbstractBackgroundHealth coaching is the process of using conversation, clinical strategies and interventions to engage clients in setting goals and identifying strategies to facilitate behaviour changes that allow clients to better self-manage their health. Health coaching is a new and growing industry in the USA.

pmc-13462677.title: eDNA Analysis of Aquatic Microcosms Reveals the Effects of a Copper Pollution Event on Sedimentary Microbial Assemblages in Freshwater Wetlands
pmc-13462677.creator: Anna S. Flynn, A. Mark Osborn, Vincent Pettigrove, Jeff Shimeta, Sara M. Long
pmc-13462677.description: Metal contamination is known to cause shifts in structure of freshwater assemblages where sensitive species do not survive and tolerant species thrive, and given their sensitivity, ubiquitous nature, and high abundances, microbes are ideal targets for biomonitoring assessments. However, the responses of diverse microbial communities to metal contamination in freshwater environments are currently understudied, particularly in the Southern hemisphere.

pmc-13540609.title: Detection and Removal of Hyper-synchronous Artifacts in Massively Parallel Spike Recordings
pmc-13540609.creator: Jonas Oberste-Frielinghaus, Aitor Morales-Gregorio, Simon Essink, Alexander Kleinjohann, Cristiano A. Köhler, Frederic Barthélemy, Alexa Riehle, Thomas Brochier, Simon Musall, Junji Ito, Sonja Grün
pmc-13540609.description: Contemporary electrophysiology experiments often involve massively parallel recordings of neuronal activity using multi-electrode arrays. While researchers have been aware of artifacts arising from electric cross-talk between channels in setups for such recordings, systematic and quantitative assessment of the effects of those artifacts on the data quality has never been reported.

pmc-13556646.title: 317. FGF-2 modulates serotonergic neuron activity via FGFR4 signaling
pmc-13556646.creator: R Paliokha, M Racicky, D Grinchii, E Dremencov
pmc-13556646.description: BackgroundFibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) displays diverse neuroactive properties. It has been shown to induce anxiolytic and antidepressant-like effects in rodents, yet it can also increase alcohol consumption, while the FGFR1 antagonist PD173074 reduces it, suggesting potential pro-addictive actions of FGF2 (Paliokha et al., Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 28:i200, 2025).

pmc-13604284.title: A Computational Histology Artificial Intelligence Prognostic Biomarker in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Using the Cancer Genome Atlas
pmc-13604284.creator: Benjamin A. Bleiberg, Masaoki Ito, Melina Marmarelis, Viswesh Krishna, Vivek Nimgaonkar, Haochen Zhang, Trevor J. Royce, Yasuhiro Tsutani, David Kozono, Charu Aggarwal
pmc-13604284.description: Simple SummaryRisk stratification to predict which non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients are likely to have poor outcomes remains challenging. We applied the previously developed Computational Histology Artificial Intelligence (CHAI) platform to identify a novel histologic biomarker in data from The Cancer Genome Atlas.

pmc-13665612.title: Machine Learning‐Based PAT Tool for Real‐Time Residual Moisture Monitoring in Lyophilized Biopharmaceuticals Using NIR Spectroscopy
pmc-13665612.creator: Samuele Fiorenza, Mariapia D'Urso, Ambra Massei, Nunzia Falco, Davide Fissore, Enza Torino
pmc-13665612.description: There is a growing demand in the pharmaceutical industry to optimize analytical methodologies, reducing time and resource consumption while ensuring rapid process development and cost‐efficient manufacturing. Indeed, Food and Drug Administration (FDA) introduced the Process Analytical Technology (PAT) as an initiative enabling manufacturers to measure and control in real‐time processes based on the Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs) of the product.
